title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 6, 2026: KOSPI Falls Below 7,000, KOSDAQ +3%
content:
KOSPI closed at 6,941.39, down 0.89%, giving back an early gain and slipping below 7,000 as chip heavyweights weakened; KOSDAQ closed at 919.92, up 2.98%, as money rotated into chip substrates and equipment, cybersecurity and HLB group stocks.

IndexCloseChange
KOSPI6,941.39-0.89%
KOSDAQ919.92+2.98%

1. Chip heavyweights weaken — KOSPI loses 7,000 while KOSDAQ surges

Korean markets opened higher on the strength of U.S. tech shares during the holiday break, but Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and other large chip names turned lower during the session and foreign and retail selling widened, erasing the early gain. KOSPI rose as high as roughly 7,044 early on, then slid to around 6,970 and back below 7,000, ending at 6,941.39 (-0.89%). KOSDAQ moved the other way, closing at 919.92 (+2.98%).

2. AI-driven hacking at financial firms — cybersecurity stocks jump

Reports of hacking and personal-data leaks involving AI agents at major banks and second-tier financial firms raised expectations of larger security spending and system replacement. Sands Lab and Raon Secure rose sharply, and buying spread to Genians, KCS, SPSoft, S2W, Ksign, ICTK, Hancom WITH and Ahnlab.

3. HLB's liver cancer drug — FDA inspection closes as VAI, HLB group stocks rally

An FDA cGMP inspection of the manufacturing facility for HLB's liver cancer drug rivoceranib reportedly closed with a VAI (Voluntary Action Indicated) classification, which means some observations were raised but no formal regulatory action is required beyond voluntary correction. Expectations for a resubmitted new drug application (NDA) grew. HLB Biostep hit its daily upper limit, and HLB Pharma, HLB Global, HLB Therapeutics, HLB Panagene, HLB Life Science and HLB also gained.

4. KOSDAQ chip names — rotation into substrates and equipment

While Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell on KOSPI, small and mid-cap chip equipment, materials and substrate stocks were strong on KOSDAQ. Some money leaving the large chip names appeared to rotate into PCB and substrate makers such as ISU Petasys, Simmtech, Korea Circuit, TLB, Daeduck Electronics and LG Innotek, and equipment names such as Jusung Engineering, Doosan Tesna and KC Tech.

5. Samsung Electro-Mechanics wins another AI server MLCC contract

Samsung Electro-Mechanics reported a 285.6 billion won supply contract for AI server MLCCs, its sixth long-term supply deal this year. Cumulative long-term contracts for AI server MLCCs, silicon capacitors and inductors now total roughly 3.9 trillion won. MLCC-related names including Kochip, Hanchem, Samwha Capacitor and Amotech were in focus.

6. Samsung SDI and EcoPro BM to co-develop solid-state battery materials

News that Samsung SDI and EcoPro BM will jointly develop core materials for solid-state batteries, targeting commercialization in 2027, drew buying across battery-related stocks. Samsung SDI, EcoPro BM, EcoPro and ISU Specialty Chemical were in focus, and TCC Steel, TSI, POSCO Future M and Sangsin EDP also rose.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI fall below 7,000 on Oct 6?
It opened higher on U.S. tech strength, but large chip stocks such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix weakened and foreign and retail selling grew, so the index gave back its gain and closed at 6,941.39 (-0.89%).

Why was KOSDAQ so strong?
Money rotated from large chip names into chip substrates and equipment, while AI-hacking news lifted cybersecurity stocks and the FDA inspection result lifted HLB group stocks. KOSDAQ closed at 919.92 (+2.98%).

What does VAI mean in an FDA inspection?
VAI (Voluntary Action Indicated) means inspectors noted some issues but no formal regulatory action is required beyond the company's voluntary correction.
